This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Stocks open lower this morning as the Commerce Department reported a modest uptick in retail
spending last month.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow fell 260 points.
Retail spending rose by two-tenths of one percent between September and October.
Consumers spent more money at gas stations and restaurants last month, but dialed back
their spending at the grocery store.
Home and garden centers also got a bump in sales in October.
Home Depot is reporting stronger than expected profits for its most recent quarter.
Home Depot also named a new CEO, promoting Richard McPhail, who had been serving as chief
financial officer.
Technical glitches caused headaches for some banking customers and air travelers on Monday,
days after outages at Microsoft and the FAA.
Authorities say the problems at JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines were not the result of
cyberattacks.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The Trump administration has issued a new rule closing a loophole on how certain foreign
countries or companies headquartered in them can buy and then rent out the power of U.S.
computer chips.
The issue is at the heart of the NVIDIA scandal.
NVIDIA makes highly sought-after computer chips.
Former NVIDIA CEO, Jensen Wong, is accused of being involved with a woman who used to
run a company called Megaspeed but was allegedly spying for China, NPR Shannon Bond has more.
On Monday, the Commerce Department announced a new rule designed to make it harder for
China to access top chips that would close this loophole that this scandal has put a
spotlight on.
And then last night, the Justice and Commerce Department confirmed they are conducting a
criminal investigation into whether Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company NVIDIA was working
with, was funneling restricted chips into China.
NPR Shannon Bond reporting.
The late civil rights and labor leader Dolores Huerta made history this week.
She became the first woman and first non-elected person to lie in honor at the California State
Capitol in Sacramento.
From member station KQED, Farida Jamfala Romero has more.
Hundreds of people, including the first Latino governor-elect in California's modern history,
walked in a procession behind a hearse carrying Huerta's casket to the Capitol Building in
Sacramento, many chanting, "Yes, we can."
Sarah Almaraz drove three hours from the city of Fresno with her 10-year-old son to pay
her respects.
"Definitely an historic moment for all of us in California, especially Latinos.
I think that what she's done has given people just the realization that everyday people have
power."
Huerta, who co-founded what became the United Farm Workers, died of cancer last month at
age 96 in Bakersfield.
For NPR News, I'm Farida Jamfala Romero in Sacramento, California.
On Wall Street, the Dow was now down about 300 points.
You're listening to NPR News.
The handwritten draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s 1963 "I Have a Dream" speech is now
on display.
It's at the National Center for Civil and Human Rights in Atlanta.
From member station WABE, Alex Helmic reports it's set to be auctioned in January.
Speechwriter Edward Clayton was one of those who helped King with the speech delivered
from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963.
Clayton's wife, civil rights advocate Zernona Clayton, discovered the handwritten draft
in the '90s in her late husband's desk, tucked inside an envelope labeled "Speech."
It includes the opening lines and powerful finish, but not the famous "I Have a Dream"
refrain, which King added spontaneously.
The draft will head to Chicago for viewing and then to New York to be auctioned off at
Christie's where they estimate it could fetch more than $10 million.
Money from the sale will go to the Zernona Clayton Foundation and the King Center in
Atlanta.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Helmic in Atlanta.
President Trump is meeting leaders of allied nations today in the Philippines.
He's met with leaders of what's called the Quad, Australia, Japan, and India.
The group was formed to balance power against China.
However, Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in coming days in a trilateral summit
with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Also today, President Trump has signed a statement with officials from Thailand.
The statement affirms that both countries will sign a trade deal.
You're listening to NPR.
